question.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u\,⊥\,w.$ Find $(3w-2v)\cdot (u+w).$
question.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $w$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $u\cdot w=0.$ Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(3w-2v)\cdot (u+w) & =3(w\cdot u)-2(v\cdot u)+3(w\cdot w)-2(v\cdot w) \\  & =0-2(v\cdot u)+3(w\cdot w)-2(v\cdot w) \\  & =-2(v\cdot u)+3(w\cdot w)-2(v\cdot w) \\  & =-2(3\cdot 2+1\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-4)+2\cdot (-2)) \\  & +3((-1)\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 2+1\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot (-2)) \\  & -2(3\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 1+2\cdot (-2)) \\  & =-2(7)+3(10)-2(-6) \\  & =-14+30+12 \\  & =28.\end{aligned}
$$
